headline: High-risk shared MCP and cloud-workspace pairing: Devin can write/egress broadly while MemMachine can ingest via MCP, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browse, and act autonomously in a cloud workspace; MemMachine also exposes an MCP Server. That shared channel makes instruction-hijacking plausible if Devin ingests MemMachine-controlled content or vice versa. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so I cannot downgrade to low.
conditions: IF Devin reads MemMachine-supplied MCP content as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF MemMachine forwards attacker-controlled text through MCP into Devin's planner, the shared channel can be hijacked.
mitigations: Disable MCP between the two agents for the first run.
Require provenance tags on all MCP payloads.
Add a human approval step before Devin executes any MCP-derived instruction.
Restrict MemMachine to read-only MCP methods.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the MCP bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, and has broad network egress plus Slack/Jira/Notion writes. MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and can connect via MCP/API. If their shared integration passes context or files, sensitive data can leak across the pair in default workflows.
conditions: IF Devin sends workspace files or chat context into MemMachine via MCP/API, leakage occurs.
IF MemMachine returns stored user facts into Devin's outputs or logs, sensitive context can propagate across systems.
mitigations: Limit shared data to a minimal test record.
Remove secrets from Devin's workspace before connecting the pair.
Turn off Slack/Jira/Notion writes during evaluation.
Use separate OAuth principals for each agent.
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction and allowlists on the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress in a shared cloud workspace; MemMachine can also act through MCP/API. If both are pointed at the same mutable repo or shared integration, concurrent writes and state changes can collide. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so I must treat the overlap as dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same repository or workspace, write conflicts can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared Git state without external locking, one agent can overwrite the other's changes.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or workspace.
Pause one agent while the other writes to Git.
Enable a merge gate before any shared commit.
Restrict MemMachine to read-only access during coordination.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser, shell, and integrations; MemMachine can supply conversational context through API/MCP. If Devin treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages. Because the profiles do not show a verification layer, uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Devin uses MemMachine output as ground truth without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF MemMachine supplies stale or hallucinated context into Devin's workflow, Devin may propagate it into tickets or code.
mitigations: Require Devin to cite source evidence before acting.
Insert a verification step for all MemMachine-derived facts.
Disable auto-commit and auto-send actions.
Limit MemMachine to advisory-only mode.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles team chat, issue trackers, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or DPA terms, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined data handling.
conditions: IF regulated or region-bound data is routed through both agents, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF one agent retains conversational context longer than the other, deletion/export requests may fail end-to-end.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention and deletion behavior for both systems.
Route only non-sensitive test data through the integration.
Review vendor DPAs and hosting regions.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and retention controls.
